transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Redwood CSM); Priya Reddy (Verdigris Eng Lead), Carlos Mendes (Verdigris CTO), Lena Wu (Verdigris Data Eng), Tom Baker (Verdigris PM)

Summary: quick hosted API walkthrough demonstrating embeddings and rerank endpoints, plus Console tips and Optimize suggestions. Customer has ML infra on GCP, uses Postgres + Elastic for metadata; primary goals: improve search relevance for product docs and reduce latency under 150ms p95 for web search.

[00:00:08] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for making time, quick intros, I'm Alex Morgan, AE. Samir is our solutions engineer, Maya handles customer success.
[00:00:18] Priya (Verdigris): Hi all, Priya here, I lead search infra. Our main thing is serving docs and product faq results, latency and cost both matter.
[00:00:26] Carlos (Verdigris): Carlos here, CTO - interested in deployment options and auditability.
[00:00:34] Samir (Redwood SE): Great, we'll run through embeddings first then a two-stage retrieval + rerank demo using the hosted API and show Console metrics and Optimize suggestions.
[00:00:48] Tom (Verdigris): quick note, we get bursts around product release, so autoscale behavior and burst cost are a thing.

[00:01:10] Alex: quick agenda - 1) embeddings endpoint and batching, 2) vector search pattern, 3) reranker endpoint, 4) Console demo, 5) Optimize recommendations and next steps.

[00:02:05] Samir: OK so embeddings. Our hosted /embeddings endpoint supports synchronous batches, you can send up to 2048 tokens per item depending on model, and we recommend 512-d or 1024-d depending on recall needs. In practice for docs we usually see good tradeoffs at 768.
[00:02:38] Priya: say more about batching - we currently create embeddings offline with a job, but we'd like to do incremental updates in real time.
[00:02:47] Samir: sure - you can do small realtime batches (1-16) with lower latency; for bulk indexing use background batches (64-512) to amortize overhead. The Console will show per-call token cost so you can experiment.
[00:03:12] Lena (Verdigris): is there a suggested chunk size for docs? we chunk by paragraph now and get inconsistent results.
[00:03:21] Samir: we often do ~200-400 token chunks and store the chunk text + metadata. Also add semantic anchors like headings in metadata.

[00:04:00] [00:04:00] Alex: demo time - Samir will walk through the API live.
[00:04:09] Samir: pasting a curl example - curl POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-v2, body: [{"text":"..."}] - response returns vectors and token counts. occasional notes: transcriber often shows model names wrong, like redwood embedder, sorry if the transcript confuses that.
[00:04:34] Speaker 2: mm-hmm

[00:05:00] Samir: moving to retrieval pattern - typical pipeline is: 1) first-pass ANN with existing vector DB (they mentioned Postgres + FAISS earlier), 2) call our /rerank endpoint with topK candidates and the original query, 3) rerank returns scores and optionally structured highlights. Rerank reduces false positives and reorders by semantic relevance.
[00:05:29] Priya: we use Milvus in staging; can Redwood accept any ANN store?
[00:05:36] Samir: yes, any ANN store works. We just need the vectors and identifiers; our rerank call expects candidate ids and original texts or snippets.

[00:06:10] Carlos: what's the latency impact? If we rerank 50 candidates, what happens to p95?
[00:06:18] Samir: good question. For hosted, a small rerank model (compact) can rerank 50 items in ~60-90ms median on our default profile; larger rerank models increase quality but add latency. We can recommend a two-tier approach: coarse rerank (cheap) then on-click expensive scoring. Also caching, prefix KV cash (sic) helps for repeated queries.
[00:06:45] Priya: KV cash?
[00:06:48] Samir: sorry, KV cache, my bad - we cache prefix key-values to avoid recomputing attention states for common prompts, it's mostly for generation but some patterns help for rerank too.

[00:07:30] [00:07:30] Alex: Console quick tour - here's per-route dashboard showing token breakdown, avg latency, and cost per 1k requests. We can filter by model variant and timeframe.
[00:07:52] Maya (Redwood CSM): you'll get cost heatmaps and we show suggestions from Redwood Optimize like enabling smaller quantized model for rerank and increasing batch size during nightly indexing.

[00:08:22] Tom: interesting, can Optimize recommend batch sizes based on our observed distribution?
[00:08:25] Maya: yes, Optimize analyzes token distribution and suggests batching/caching profiles and a quantization plan. It also simulates expected cost impact.

[00:09:05] Priya: security - we need SOC2, audit logs, SSO and the ability to restrict data to region.
[00:09:12] Alex: we are SOC2 type 2, we provide audit logs and SSO/SAML integration, and for data residency we have region pins; private deployments (VPC) are available for enterprise customers. We'll share the security pack after the call.

[00:10:10] [00:10:10] Carlos: do you keep customer data for training? that's a concern for us.
[00:10:14] Alex: hosted option has a config to opt out of model training and to disable retention; dedicated/private options provide more strict isolation and we can sign data handling terms.

[00:11:00] Samir: back to rerank API - sample payload: POST /v1/rerank {"query": "...","candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"..."}, ...], "model":"redwood-rerank-v1"} returns scores, explanation tokens, and can include reranked snippets. We demo live with Verdigris sample set.
[00:11:42] [00:11:42] Samir: running demo run - sending 25 candidates, model=compact-rerank, request returned in 78ms, scores look sensible.
[00:12:05] Priya: can we get structured outputs like category tags?
[00:12:12] Samir: yes - you can request structured outputs and use function-like calls to map to categories, or run a lightweight classification model on top of rerank results.

[00:13:00] Lena: about evaluation - how do we measure improvement? we have click-through and ranking metrics but need something reproducible.
[00:13:09] Alex: we suggest an offline eval harness: sample queries, human labels, MAP/NDCG, and also run online A/B with canary rollout in Console. We'll share our eval spreadsheet.

[00:14:30] [00:14:30] Tom: pricing - ballpark for hosted rerank + embeddings for our scale (100M tokens/month).
[00:14:38] Alex: ballpark depends on model sizes and batching. We'll send tailored pricing but initial estimate is dominated by tokenization for large indexing and by per-call compute for rerank. / We'll include examples in the pricing sheet.

[00:15:50] [00:15:50] Priya: question on model variants - can we pin a stable model for production while experimenting with newer ones?
[00:15:58] Samir: yes, Console supports version pinning and rollout policies (canary/A-B) and automatic fallback if a variant fails.

[00:16:30] [00:16:30] Speaker 1: hmm

[00:16:45] Samir: Optimize suggestion: quantize rerank model to int8 for night bulk reranks, keep int16 or fp16 for low-latency web requests. This can cut cost by ~30-45% depending on workloads.
[00:17:10] Priya: any accuracy loss with quantization?
[00:17:14] Samir: small, we run evals to compare; Optimize will flag regressions against baseline prompts automatically.

[00:18:20] [00:18:20] Alex: now a little on autoscaling - hosted has burst pools and we expose autoscale settings; Dedicated gives stronger guarantees with reserved GPUs. For Verdigris we'd probably start hosted with burst capacity and move to Dedicated if predictability and latency guarantees are required.
[00:18:50] Carlos: what's the SLA for hosted?
[00:18:53] Alex: hosted has best-effort SLAs currently; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. We'll map SLA needs in the pilot.

[00:19:40] Lena: network - can Redwood operate inside our VPC with private peering?
[00:19:44] Alex: yes, Private has VPC peering and on-prem options; for hosted we have IP allowlists and private link in some regions.

[00:20:30] [00:20:30] Samir: demo deep-dive: here's a sample pipeline in Console - ingestion job writes embeddings to your vector DB then we call rerank on topK=30. Console shows token distribution and suggests batch size 128 for nightly jobs.
[00:21:05] Priya: what's the recommended topK? 30 vs 100?
[00:21:10] Samir: start with 30 for quality/latency balance, increase to 100 if recall needs it; rerank cost scales linearly with topK.

[00:22:00] [00:22:00] Tom: can rerank return provenance, like which chunk matched?
[00:22:04] Samir: yes, we return candidate ids and score breakdowns; you can surface provenance and highlight spans.

[00:23:15] Alex: quick note on observability - trace ids per request, token-level breakdown, and we can push trace to your S3 for retention.

[00:24:00] [00:24:00] Priya: latency SLO is a hard constraint for UI search - p95 < 150ms.
[00:24:06] Samir: for that SLO we'd recommend compact rerank + aggressive caching + client side optimistic results with background rerank for reordering. Also prefix caching for hot queries.

[00:25:30] Carlos: curious about costs during peak release windows - will autoscale cause unpredictably large bills?
[00:25:37] Alex: you can set burst caps and quota alerts; Optimize can simulate cost for peak patterns so budgeting is easier.

[00:26:45] [00:26:45] Maya: action item recap will be shared in CRM and in the follow-up email.

[00:27:10] Priya: any red flags around integrating our stack? we use GKE and Airflow.
[00:27:17] Samir: no major issues - we have Airflow operators, a Python SDK, and k8s-friendly clients. We'll share integration examples.

[00:28:30] [00:28:30] Live Q/A segment - Priya asks about cold-starts for small batches.
[00:28:37] Samir: cold-starts can be 100-200ms for tiny batches depending on model; we mitigate with pooling and warmers.

[00:29:50] Priya: is there a trial org we can use with sample quotas?
[00:29:54] Alex: yes we'll provision a sandbox org and API key for the pilot.

[00:30:40] [00:30:40] Demo: Samir runs an A/B rerank comparison with baseline lexical rank vs Redwood rerank; shows improved NDCG on sample test set.

[00:31:55] Lena: we'll need a CSV of evaluation results to share with stakeholders - can you format that?
[00:32:02] Samir: yes, we'll export a spreadsheet template and populate initial numbers from the benchmark.

[00:33:30] Tom: procurement - we'll need security docs and a draft contract before pilot.
[00:33:37] Alex: noted, we'll attach security pack, standard pilot agreement, and also a procurement checklist.

[00:34:50] [00:34:50] Priya: any gotchas with multi-language docs? we have docs in EN, FR, DE.
[00:34:57] Samir: embeddings support unicode and multi-lingual models; Optimize can analyze per-language token distributions and recommend model variants if you need language-specific tuning.

[00:36:10] [00:36:10] Alex: timeline - customer suggested pilot within 2 weeks, then a 4-week eval.

[00:36:22] Priya: yes we'd like start Feb 2 if possible.

[00:36:30] Samir: technical note - for PII we recommend token redaction pre-ingest or redact at query time depending on use case.

[00:37:45] [00:37:45] Carlos: what's the rollback story if a model change causes regressions?
[00:37:50] Samir: Console supports instant rollback to pinned version and we can auto-revert on regression alerts.

[00:38:55] [00:38:55] Alex: recap of next steps: sandbox org, pricing, security pack, benchmarks.

[00:39:20] Maya: I'll send a follow-up with links to docs: embedding playbook, rerank API reference, Optimize guide (links in email).

[00:40:00] [00:40:00] Priya: thanks all, a couple of small clarifications on the payload shape after the meeting would be helpful.

[00:40:15] Samir: noted we'll include example payloads and a small test harness.

[00:41:30] [00:41:30] Short wrap Q/A.

[00:42:00] Alex: ok final recap and we'll assign tasks—see action items.

[00:43:00] [00:43:00] Meeting ends, recording stops.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cash), some speaker labels generic (Speaker 1/2) due to call platform. Referenced artifacts: embedding-eval-template.xlsx (shared), security-pack.pdf (shared), sandbox invite link (to be sent).
